tagline: Church walls and a house that leaned with the trees.
intro: Old Sheldon Church Road runs about seven miles through Beaufort County between Gardens Corner and Yemassee, under oak canopies and past Lowcountry wetlands. The old parish church survives along it as walls among oaks and scattered graves. Its ruin has more than one account of how it came to be.

Near Yemassee, Auldbrass makes a separate architectural excursion. Frank Lloyd Wright set its walls at a slant to echo the local trees, using cypress and cedar from the nearby swamp. Right angles had little part in the design.

moments.title: Old Sheldon Church Ruins
moments.text: Oaks and scattered graves surround the surviving walls of the former Prince William’s Parish Church.

moments.title: Auldbrass
moments.text: Slanting wooden walls and copper roofs give Wright’s plantation complex the angles he found in the native trees.
